findings.impact: Digest and logical-byte equality do not fix physical allocation. The cap enforced for new publication is not enforced for existing-result reuse, so a success receipt can exceed the externally bound persistent output cap.
findings.recommended_fix: Use the same directory plus max(st_size,st_blocks*512) allocation check on every existing/reuse and final return path, with a private KEEP_SIZE regression; retain byte/SHA equality checks. No change to original M33/single-job code is needed.
findings.reproduction: A private synthetic four-file summary completed within4MiB. Linux fallocate(FALLOC_FL_KEEP_SIZE) then reserved cap+65536 bytes on the private per_seed_core.csv. Its size, contents and every summary file SHA stayed unchanged. Total directory/file allocation grew from417792 to4296704 bytes, exceeding4194304. execute_summary reuse still returned success with the original complete SHA.
findings.title: Existing completed namespace reuse skips actual allocation cap

original_requested_comparisons.case: Failure unlinking a stage after completion
original_requested_comparisons.scope: Injected Path.unlink failure during private create/reentry had zero calls; the four-member publication remained valid and same complete SHA reused.

original_requested_comparisons.case: Legal cpu_slot mutation in complete accepted on reuse
original_requested_comparisons.scope: M5 complete has no cpu_slot field. Adding a legal value changes exact expected complete bytes and is refused; runtime invocation slot is outside completion identity.
